risks.basis: Stated directly in [P2] (Item 1A) regarding regulatory caps, routing mandates, and potential impacts; fee independence stated in [P1] (Item 1) and [P2] (Item 1A); fiscal 2026 net revenue growth stated in [P3] (Item 7).
risks.claim: Expanding global regulation of interchange reimbursement fees, merchant discount rates, network fees, and routing rules could reduce Visa's payments volume, limit products, and raise compliance costs.
quotes: Regulators worldwide are expanding their authority over the payments industry, including IRFs, MDRs, network fees, operating rules, and related practices.

Recent conflicting federal court decisions on the validity of Regulation II's interchange fee standard have created additional uncertainty and could result in a significantly lower interchange cap for debit transactions.

quotes: Governments in numerous jurisdictions seek to strengthen domestic control over payments infrastructure and reduce reliance on international payment providers like Visa, through market access barriers, preferential domestic regulations, localization requirements and support for domestic systems.
Central banks in numerous countries are developing or expanding national RTP networks, with some exploring cross-border RTP connectivity.

For example, the ECB has launched the European Payments Initiative's pan-European A2A payment system and a multi-year effort to explore a digital euro, as an alternative to foreign digital currency and payment service providers.

Our reliance on third-party AI tools, models, infrastructure and data processing environments may further limit our ability to monitor, control or remediate how confidential or personal information is accessed, retained, used, transferred or secured.
As agentic commerce scales, there could be increased instances of unauthorized, erroneous or disputed payments, or fraud.

risks.claim: Pending antitrust and civil litigation—with estimated unresolved U.S. covered litigation interchange claims of $15.9 billion and a fiscal 2026 GAAP litigation provision of $1,764 (table in millions)—could cause material losses or force operating-rule changes.
quotes: In the event we are found liable or reach a settlement in any action, particularly in a large class action lawsuit, such as one involving an antitrust claim entitling the plaintiff to treble damages in the U.S., or we incur liability arising from a government investigation, we may be required to pay significant awards or judgments, settlements, costs or fines.

The failure of one or both of the retrospective responsibility plans to adequately insulate us from the impact of such settlements, judgments, losses or liabilities could materially harm our financial condition or cash flows, or even cause us to become insolvent.

The interchange at issue for unresolved claims will continue to increase.

risks.basis: Stated in [P2] (Item 1A) regarding competitive and stablecoin/AI disintermediation threats; Visa's product initiatives and fiscal 2026 value-added services growth stated in [P1] (Item 1) and [P3] (Item 7).

risks.basis: Stated in [P2] (Item 1A) and [P3] (Item 7, Effective Income Tax Rate).
